claims.summary: For X_1..X_N i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2, kappa > 0 fixed, l_1 the Leighton-Shor scale, D(g) = sum_i g(X_i) - N int g, c > 0 and a family F_N of at most N^c unions of cells of side 2^(-l_1) fixed before the points are drawn, with probability tending to one, for every dyadic delta_0 with kappa sqrt(log N/N) <= delta_0 <= 2^(-l_1): (a) every union A of cells of side delta_0, every union S of cells of side 2^(-l_1), every dyadic W = 2^(-k) in [2^(-l_1), 1] and every set T of W-cells whose union contains the symmetric difference of A and S have |D(1_A) - D(1_S)| <= c_kappa sqrt(N log N) P(A) + L sqrt N ((2(l_1 - k) + 5)^(3/4) + sqrt(log N))(P(A) + P(S) + 12 W #T), P the inner perimeter, c_kappa and L the constants of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound and lem:tube-localized-discrepancy; (b) every S in F_N has |D(1_S)| <= P(S) sqrt((c+3) N log N) + (c+3) log N, and for any family of M_N unions of coarse cells fixed in advance, |D(1_S)| <= P(S) sqrt(N(log M_N + 3 log N)) + log M_N + 3 log N; (c) for every beta > 0 and w in [2^(-l_1), 1], every weighted sum sum_k a_k 1_{A_k} of unions of fine cells with P(A_k) > 0, each with a guide S_k in F_N, a dyadic W_k in [2^(-l_1), w] and a set T_k of W_k-cells covering the symmetric difference, with P(S_k) + 12 W_k #T_k <= beta P(A_k), has |D| <= C sqrt N ((2 log_2(w 2^(l_1)) + 5)^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)) sum_k |a_k| P(A_k), C = c_kappa + L(1 + beta) + beta sqrt(c+3) + (c+3)/kappa; (d) at (4,4) a nested chain y delta_0 sum_k 1_{A_k} of such layers at level y >= 2e^16 with discrete cost at most 2 has |D| <= C sqrt N T((2 log_2(w 2^(l_1)) + 5)^(3/4) + sqrt(log N)), T = 8 (log(y/2))^(-1/4), for every number of layers, and |D| <= 23 C sqrt(N log N) for N large when log(w 2^(l_1)) <= (log N)^(2/3)(log(y/2))^(1/3).
claims.assessment: Working proof: (a) lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (a) at the Leighton-Shor mesh, then lem:tube-localized-discrepancy (b) for E 1_A - 1_S, which vanishes on the coarse cells outside the union of T, with inner variation at most P(A) + P(S), boundary ring at most 4W #T and extra term at most 8W #T; (b) Bernstein for the binomial count with variance at most N P(S)^2/2 by the relative isoperimetry of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound's entry on the unit square, and a union over the family; (c) linearity, (a) and (b) per layer, the additive log N charged to P(A_k) >= delta_0; (d) the nesting identity and lem:fine-grid-leighton-shor (c) for sum_k P(A_k) <= T/(y delta_0), and arithmetic.
claims.rationale: On dyadic grids against Lebesgue measure, sets near guides from a polynomial family fixed in advance cost the tube factor (log(w 2^(l_1)))^(3/4) per unit perimeter, and at (4,4) nested chains of any number of layers whose layers lie within tubes of width w <= 2^(-l_1) exp((log N)^(2/3)(log(y/2))^(1/3)) of such guides, with guide and tube lengths at most beta times each layer's perimeter, are at most C sqrt(N log N): the fifth review's outcome (A) for such chains, beyond lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (d), which needs K <= N^(1/7), and lem:discrete-flow-bound (c), which loses up to (log N)^(1/8).
claims.next_action: Nested unions of translates of one Leighton-Shor set, whose back boundary has multiplicity K and which lem:discrete-flow-bound (c) charges (log(K y))^(1/4) above the conjectured order: decide whether the front boundaries add coherently, given that the cost bounds the back boundary's share of the variation by 8 (log(K y/2))^(-1/4).

relationships: Its (a) at the Leighton-Shor mesh, its relative isoperimetry for (b), and the nesting identity of its (c).
Part (b) on the difference of the coarse averages and the guide.
Its (c) bounds the total variation of a chain at level y.
Its (c) bounds chains of multiplicity m at C sqrt(N log N)(1 + (log(m y))^(1/4)); part (d) here bounds guided chains of any multiplicity without that factor. Neither implies the other.

At (4,4) on dyadic grids, against Lebesgue measure: guided chains of any number of layers are at most C sqrt(N log N); a bound of the goal's smeared form, through lem:smeared-y-term (b), only for class functions whose cell averages are such chains.
